sources.title: Structured Kuaishou interview note containing the K-smallest prompt
Tagged repository question record for K smallest array elements
Deterministic Java validation against full-sort-prefix oracle

claims.text: The recovered source says only to find K smallest elements in an array and does not specify distinctness, result ordering, input mutation, or invalid-K behavior; the candidate explicitly declares those implementation contracts.

With a max-heap capped at K, after each processed prefix the heap contains that prefix's K smallest values under multiplicity semantics; the heap maximum is exactly the boundary candidate that can be replaced by a smaller new value.
The implementation preserves duplicate occurrences, does not mutate input, and sorts only the final K candidates to provide a deterministic ascending output under the candidate's declared contract.
The capped-heap scan costs O(n log K) time and O(K) heap space; ascending output adds O(K log K) sorting, while an unordered result can omit that final sort.
Using Comparator.reverseOrder rather than subtraction avoids an overflow-prone integer comparator on MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE inputs.

Eight fixed cases and 5000 fixed-seed arrays match an independent oracle that fully sorts a copy then takes its first K values; tests also verify source immutability and explicit invalid-input behavior.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=8 randomized=5000 oracle=full-sort-prefix input_immutable=true invalid_k=fail-fast
checks: duplicate multiplicity, negative values, and integer extremes
5000 fixed-seed arrays match a full-sort-prefix oracle
null, negative K, and K greater than length fail fast

boundary_tests.expected: empty result or complete sorted result

findings: The source-first boundary is preserved: distinctness, result order, mutation, and invalid-K behavior are declared candidate contracts rather than attributed to the original interview note.
The max-heap choice is justified by the replacement boundary and is accompanied by a prefix invariant rather than a memorized Top-K slogan.
Duplicate multiplicity is explicitly covered, preventing accidental Set semantics.
The implementation avoids subtraction-based comparator overflow and the fixed tests include integer extremes.
The deterministic oracle uses full sorting rather than reproducing the heap algorithm, and randomized coverage checks input immutability as a separate property.
The answer distinguishes heap, full-sort, and Quickselect tradeoffs without pretending the source required one specific algorithm.
No project or production claims are fabricated.
Required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
